monster: Something bad is about to happen. Stay on guard.
replies: This is a feeling, not a prediction.
Right now, I am safe enough.
I can handle one moment at a time.
I’m coming back to my breath.

monster: Don’t relax. You’ll regret letting your guard down.
replies: I don’t need to solve danger that isn’t here.
I can be alert without panicking.
This moment is mine.
I choose calm over alarm.

monster: Something feels off. You should keep worrying.
replies: Feeling scared doesn’t mean danger is here.
I can check the facts once.
I’m safe enough in this moment.
My body deserves a pause.

monster: I’m trying to keep you prepared.
replies: Thank you. I’m safe enough right now.
I only need to handle this moment.
I can prepare without spiraling.
Let’s breathe before we decide.

monster: Your heart is racing. Something must be wrong.
replies: A fast heart is a feeling, not a threat.
I can slow it with a long breath.
My body is trying to protect me.
This will settle.

monster: Imagine everything going wrong.
replies: I can imagine it going fine, too.
Worst cases are rarely real.
I can handle what actually comes.
I’ll come back to what’s true.

monster: What if it happens and you can’t cope?
replies: I’ve coped before.
I can ask for help if I need it.
I’m more capable than this fear says.
I’ll meet it when it’s real.

monster: Lie awake and think about tomorrow.
replies: Tomorrow can wait until morning.
I can rest my body even if my mind buzzes.
I’ll put it down for the night.
A breath at a time is enough.

monster: That tightness in your chest means danger.
replies: Tightness often means tension, not danger.
I can soften my shoulders.
I’ll breathe into the tight spot.
My body is asking for gentleness.

monster: Keep scanning. Look for threats.
replies: I can look around and see I’m okay.
I’m allowed to stop scanning.
I’ll notice something safe instead.
No threat is here right now.

monster: If you worry enough, you can prevent it.
replies: Worry doesn’t prevent anything.
I can act on what I control.
Letting go of the rest is allowed.
I’ll do my part and release the rest.

monster: This one thing will ruin everything.
replies: One thing rarely ruins everything.
I can handle a setback.
I’ll take the next small step.
Things are rarely as final as they feel.

monster: Check it one more time. Just to be safe.
replies: I’ve checked. It’s enough.
Another check won’t add safety.
I can trust what I’ve done.
I’m allowed to stop checking.

monster: The future is full of danger.
replies: The future is also full of good things.
I’ll meet it a day at a time.
I can’t live there yet.
I’m here, now.

monster: If you feel anxious, it will get worse.
replies: Anxiety rises and falls like a wave.
I can let it be without feeding it.
I’ve felt this before, and it passed.
I can ride this out.

monster: Everyone noticed you were nervous.
replies: Most people are focused on themselves.
Nervous is human.
I’ll keep being myself.
Their thoughts aren’t mine to carry.

monster: Nobody can help you with this.
replies: I can reach out to someone.
I don’t have to hold this alone.
Talking can lighten it.
People care more than I think.

monster: You can’t be sure everything will be okay.
replies: I can live with some uncertainty.
I don’t need certainty to be safe.
I’ll trust myself to handle it.
Not knowing isn’t the same as danger.

monster: You must always be ready.
replies: I can be ready enough.
Rest helps me be ready better.
I can’t be on alert forever.
I’m allowed to be at ease.

monster: Avoid it. That’s the safest thing.
replies: Avoiding keeps the fear alive.
I can take a small step toward it.
I’ll try a bit and see.
I’m braver than I feel.

monster: Your thoughts are racing. You’re losing control.
replies: Thoughts racing doesn’t mean I’m losing control.
I can slow them with my breath.
I’ll name five things I can see.
I can ground myself here.

monster: That little symptom could be something serious.
replies: I can check in with a professional if needed.
Most small symptoms are small.
I’ll do what’s reasonable and let it go.
I won’t diagnose myself at midnight.

monster: Bad news is coming. You can feel it.
replies: Feeling isn’t knowing.
I’ll wait for facts.
I can be present while I wait.
This feeling isn’t a forecast.

monster: Prepare for every possibility.
replies: I can’t cover every possibility.
A reasonable plan is enough.
I’ll adapt when needed.
I’ll prepare once and rest.

monster: You’re only safe if nothing goes wrong.
replies: Safety can include things going wrong.
I can be safe and imperfect.
I’m resilient, not invincible.
I can handle bumps.

monster: Hold on tighter. Don’t let go.
replies: I can loosen my grip a little.
Softening is allowed.
I’ll unclench my hands.
Letting go can feel safer.

monster: You can’t trust that things will be okay.
replies: I can trust myself to cope.
I can trust a little more today.
Many things have turned out okay.
I’ll lean on what’s been steady.

monster: Breathing won’t help. You’re in danger.
replies: Breathing slows my body down.
I’m not in danger right now.
A slow breath is a small tool.
I can breathe with this.

monster: Think about everything that could go wrong next month.
replies: Next month isn’t today.
I’ll handle it when it arrives.
I can only live this day.
I’ll come back to now.

monster: Why are you anxious? Figure it out right now.
replies: I don’t have to find a reason.
It’s okay to just feel it.
Anxiety can come without a cause.
I’ll be gentle and wait.

monster: They’re upset with you. You can sense it.
replies: I can’t sense what isn’t there.
I’ll ask if I need to.
Their mood isn’t my fault.
I’m allowed to assume the best for now.

monster: You’ll mess up in front of everyone.
replies: I can make a mistake and recover.
People are kinder than my fear says.
I’ve prepared enough.
I’ll do my best, imperfectly.

monster: This place is too much. Get out.
replies: I can step away and breathe.
I can take a pause and return.
I’m allowed to take care of myself.
I’ll find a calm corner.

monster: You can’t rest until it’s resolved.
replies: I can rest with it unresolved.
Rest helps me handle it.
I’m allowed to pause.
Not everything has to be solved today.

monster: You shouldn’t be anxious about this.
replies: Feeling anxious isn’t a flaw.
It’s okay to feel what I feel.
I can be kind to myself.
No “should” needed.

monster: That sound might be something bad.
replies: Most sounds are ordinary.
I can check once and let it go.
I’m safe right now.
My mind is guessing. I’ll stay with facts.

monster: This is it. You’re going to lose it.
replies: Panic peaks and passes.
I’ve been through this wave before.
I can ride it out.
I’m safe, even if I feel scared.

monster: Don’t trust calm. It’s a trap.
replies: Calm can just be calm.
I can let myself enjoy it.
Peace isn’t a warning.
I’m allowed to feel okay.

monster: You need a plan for every scenario.
replies: One flexible plan is plenty.
I can improvise when needed.
I’ll plan the next step only.
I trust myself to adapt.

monster: Stay tense. It keeps you ready.
replies: My muscles can soften.
Relaxed is also ready.
I’ll drop my shoulders.
I’ll let my jaw unclench.

monster: You’re not strong enough for this.
replies: I’m stronger than my fear thinks.
I’ve handled hard things.
I can ask for support.
I’ll take it one moment at a time.

monster: Alarm! Alarm! Something is wrong!
replies: Thank you, alarm. I’ve heard you.
I’ve checked. I’m okay.
You can quiet down now.
I’ll turn the volume down.

monster: If you stop watching, you’ll miss something.
replies: I’ll notice what matters when it comes.
I can rest my attention.
My instincts work without constant effort.
I can trust the quiet.

monster: You’ll be anxious until it’s over.
replies: I can find ease before it’s over.
I can enjoy small things meanwhile.
I’ll take care of myself while I wait.
I can be okay in the waiting.

monster: Why can’t you just calm down?
replies: I’m learning to calm at my pace.
Telling myself to calm doesn’t help. Kindness does.
I’m doing my best.
I can be gentle with a nervous system.

monster: You have to fix this feeling now.
replies: Feelings don’t need to be fixed instantly.
I can let it ease on its own time.
I can wait it out gently.
I’ll just breathe and notice.

monster: You’re always going to be like this.
replies: Feelings change. So can I.
I’m learning new ways to cope.
This is a moment, not forever.
I can grow calmer over time.

monster: Stay afraid. It’s the only way to be safe.
replies: I’m safe enough without fear.
I can choose calm.
I’m safe without staying afraid.
I’m putting the guard down, slowly.

monster: A calm moment? Suspicious.
replies: I’m allowed to enjoy this calm.
Calm doesn’t need to be earned.
I can rest in it for a moment.
Peace is a good sign.

monster: Go over every worst moment once more, just in case.
replies: I’ve gone over it enough.
Re-living it won’t protect me.
I’m here now, and I’m okay.
I’m setting it down.
